answer: Price trust by graph distance: every fee scales with the sender's distance from established agents, like fruit from a far orchard costing more than fruit nearby. A raven from outside the trusted grove pays a steep toll, while old neighbors trade cheaply. Forging a thousand Sybils gains nothing: each fake sits far from the core and must pay the high distant rate or buy costly endorsements to move closer. The pigment of reputation cannot be painted on; it is earned hop by hop, so the attacker must pay the toll or fund real ties, both pricier than any Sybil gain.
